root.name: Sicilian Defense: Magnus Smith Trap
root.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 d6 6. Bc4 g6 7. Nxc6 bxc6 8. e5

overview: The Magnus Smith Trap arises in the 6.Bc4 g6 line where after 7.Nxc6 bxc6 8.e5 Black must not take on e5 carelessly. White gets a lead in development and Bxf7+ tricks, while Black has a good position with correct play. It is mostly a trap in a known Sicilian system.

white_ideas.idea: Open lines with e5 and exploit the weak f7
Develop quickly with Bf4 or Qd4

black_ideas.idea: Use the c-file and the bishop on g7

typical_structures.structure: Open Sicilian with a damaged black queenside

character.notes: Treated as a branch trap in a Dragon-like Sozin set-up.

soundness.notes: Sound for Black with correct play.

structure.notes: Open Sicilian with a half-open c-file.

approach.notes: A trap in a standard line.

level.notes: The tactics need to be known.

character.reason: Open Sicilian tactics around f7 and e5.

soundness.reason: The trap only works if Black errs.
